topic: Flow Separation Stalling, behavior of aircraft before and after stall
syllabus_extract: Flow Separation Stalling, behavior of aircraft before and after stall. Factors effecting stalling speed, high incidences stall, high speed stall, G stall, wing tip stall, Basic stalling speed.
specific_objectives: 6.1.2.1 Trainee will be able to describe various types of aerofoil sections, conditions of performance, theories, and concept related with performance

intro_questions: What is the primary cause of an aerodynamic stall?
Define the critical angle of attack.
How does increasing weight affect the basic stalling speed?

summary_questions: Explain the difference between a high incidence stall and a high speed stall.
Describe the specific behavior of an aircraft immediately after a wing tip stall occurs.
List three factors that influence the basic stalling speed of an aircraft.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note comparing the stall characteristics of a high-lift aerofoil section versus a low-lift section, referencing the concepts covered in LP 19 regarding power requirements.
